q1: WITH S AS (SELECT ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR FROM TAKES NATURAL JOIN SECTION GROUP BY ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR HAVING COUNT(TIME_SLOT_ID) > 4) SELECT DISTINCT ID, NAME FROM S NATURAL JOIN STUDENT
q2: WITH S AS (SELECT ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR FROM TAKES NATURAL JOIN SECTION GROUP BY ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR HAVING COUNT(TIME_SLOT_ID) > 5) SELECT DISTINCT ID, NAME FROM S NATURAL JOIN STUDENT

q2_prompt_sql: WITH S AS (SELECT ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR FROM TAKES NATURAL JOIN SECTION GROUP BY ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR HAVING COUNT(TIME_SLOT_ID) > 5) SELECT DISTINCT ID, NAME FROM S NATURAL JOIN STUDENT
counterexample: INSERT INTO SECTION (COURSE_ID, SEC_ID, YEAR, BUILDING, ROOM_NUMBER, TIME_SLOT_ID) VALUES (1, 1, 2020, 'Bldg1', 101, 1), (1, 2, 2020, 'Bldg1', 102, 2), (1, 3, 2020, 'Bldg1', 103, 3), (1, 4, 2020, 'Bldg1', 104, 4), (1, 5, 2020, 'Bldg1', 105, 5);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because the HAVING clause in the common table expression (CTE) S has different conditions. Q1 filters for IDs that have more than 4 time slots, while Q2 filters for IDs that have more than 5 time slots. This difference in the number of time slots affects the output of the queries.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when an ID has exactly 5 time slots in the SECTION table.
